details: Real GDP growth in Q1 2026 reached an annualized 2.1%, a rebound from 0.5% in Q4 2025. Personal income and consumption expenditures both increased by 0.7% in May 2026. The labor market is stable with low layoffs, and recession fears are receding, as evidenced by US Bank lowering its 12-month recession probability to 25%. This resilient economic activity could give the Federal Reserve less reason to cut interest rates aggressively, which has historically been a positive catalyst for crypto markets.
title: US Economy Shows Signs of Firming, Reducing Aggressive Fed Rate Cut Incentives

details: Bitcoin experienced a dip on July 16, 2026, extending its retreat after briefly hitting $65,000 earlier in the week. This decline is attributed to ongoing U.S.-Iran tensions and signals of less aggressive interest rate cuts from the Federal Reserve, despite softer-than-expected June inflation data. The probability of the Fed leaving interest rates unchanged in July increased to 90%, and the probability of a rate hike in December decreased.
title: Bitcoin Slips Amid Geopolitical Tensions and Hawkish Rate Cues

details: Ethereum fell approximately 4% in the past 24 hours to around $1,835 after briefly topping $1,930 earlier in the week, indicating short-term volatility. While some analysts see potential for a near-term upside, there's a warning that any recovery could be followed by a deeper correction before a new bull cycle. Upcoming US jobless claims and comments from New York Fed President John Williams could influence rate expectations and risk assets, including crypto.
title: Ethereum Sees Volatility as Analysts Eye Potential Recovery and Risks
